The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

1	# NovaPay Salary Advance — Product Reference
     2	
     3	A one-page reference so you can focus on design, not on inventing a lending model. Treat these as the rules of the product. Where something isn't specified, make a reasonable assumption and state it.
     4	
     5	> NovaPay is a fictional digital wallet used for this exercise. The numbers below are illustrative but internally consistent — design as if they're real.
     6	
     7	## What it is
     8	
     9	A short-term **salary advance**: a small amount of cash to help a salaried user bridge to their next payday. Short tenor, fixed fee, single repayment pulled on payday.
    10	
    11	## Loan tiers
    12	
    13	| Tier | Amount (PKR) |
    14	|------|--------------|
    15	| 1 | 5,000 |
    16	| 2 | 10,000 |
    17	| 3 | 15,000 |
    18	
    19	A user's offered limit is the highest tier they qualify for. They can take any amount up to that limit (in the tiers above). Requesting more than the offered limit is **not allowed** — that's one of the hard moments you'll design for.
    20	
    21	## Cost & repayment
    22	
    23	- **Fixed fee** per advance: **3% of the amount disbursed**, charged once (not monthly interest). Example: a Rs 10,000 advance costs Rs 300, so the user repays **Rs 10,300**.
    24	- **Tenor:** repaid in full on the user's **next payday** (assume ~2–4 weeks out; the exact date is known at offer time).
    25	- **Total cost of credit** (amount + fee) and the **repayment date** must be clear at the moment of decision. (See "Trust rules.")
    26	- A "haircut" can apply: the amount actually disbursed may be lower than requested if risk checks warrant it.
    27	
    28	## Decisions
    29	
    30	- **Approved** — an offer is available; the user can accept.
    31	- **Declined** — no offer. Reasons we surface internally: `credit_score`, `income_unverified`, `other`. How (and how honestly) a decline is communicated to the user is a design decision.
    32	- Income may or may not be **verified** at application (bank statement / payslip). Unverified income is a common decline reason.
    33	
    34	## Repayment outcomes (post-disbursement)
    35	
    36	- **on_time** — repaid on or before the due date.
    37	- **late** — repaid after the due date (we track days late).
    38	- **default** — 30+ days past due. A user with an active late/overdue advance is a sensitive state to design for (reminders, what they see, tone).
    39	
    40	## Trust matters most here
    41	
    42	NovaPay operates in a market where predatory digital-lending apps have harmed users and drawn regulatory action — and lending is the highest-trust moment in the whole app. How you earn (or lose) that trust is the heart of this exercise: what you show, when you show it, and how you handle the moments that don't go well. We're deliberately not giving you a checklist — those calls are yours to make and defend.
    43	
    44	## Glossary (mirrors the dataset fields, for context)
    45	
    46	`applied_amount` · `disbursed_amount` (may be < applied) · `decision` (approved/denied) · `denial_reason` · `repayment_status` (on_time/late/default) · `days_late` · `income_verified` · `income_source` (salaried/freelance).
     1	# My Problem Understanding
     2	The salary advance was shipped fast and it shows at the hard moments: telling someone what an advance will cost, that they've been declined, or that a repayment is coming due. It converts fine, but the manager doesn't want to scale something that feels predatory. My job is to make those moments honest, even where that costs some conversion.
     3	
     4	> v1 of this read was written by me without AI. This version (v2) was rewritten with the help of AI after an AI critique; I edited it, and every call in it is mine. The critique and my responses are in the table at the end.
     5	
     6	## What I'm working from
     7	I haven't seen the live flow. The starter has one home card ("You may qualify for a NovaPay salary advance" / "See your offer"), and its button only shows a TODO toast. So this section is evidence plus the risks I'm designing against, not things I observed.
     8	
     9	**Evidence**
    10	- **The manager's message:** "converts fine but feels off at the edges: the terms, the decline screen, the repayment reminders." Success is being measured by conversion.
    11	- **The brief:** shipped fast; the hard moments are cost, decline, and a repayment coming due.
    12	- **The product reference:**
    13	  - The payout can be lower than requested.
    14	  - Decline reasons are internal codes, and how honestly to explain them is "a design decision".
    15	  - Total cost and the due date "must be clear at the moment of decision".
    16	- **The starter card:** "See your **offer**" claims an offer already exists. ("You may qualify" is only a hedge.) The card is shown to everyone, right under a low balance (Rs 4,250).
    17	
    18	**Risks I'm designing against**
    19	- **Entry:** the card implies an offer exists and nudges people when their balance is low. It should reflect the user's real situation (eligible, needs verification, already has an advance, late).
    20	- **Cost:** a fee shown only as a % is hard to judge. Each tier should show the fee in rupees, the total and the due date. A tier above the limit should explain why, not throw an error.
    21	- **Accept:** a vague action ("Continue") taking out a loan, consent bundled or pre-ticked, nothing to show what was agreed afterwards. Also everything after the tap: processing, a double tap, a network failure, and a reduced payout arriving after the user has already said yes.
    22	- **Repayment:** reminders that pressure, notifications that expose the debt, collection that drains the wallet, and consequences explained too late.
    23	
    24	## What's working
    25	- It converts, so people want it. That doesn't prove they understand it.
    26	- A fixed one-time fee is simpler to understand than interest that grows. (from the product reference, not observed)
    27	- Repayment is tied to payday, with a single repayment. (from the product reference, not observed)
    28	- The three tiers are simple choices; no slider, no free-text amount.
    29	- Amounts are formatted consistently through one component.
    30	
    31	## My position on conversion
    32	I accept lower conversion in these places, on purpose:
    33	1. Full cost and due date on the same screen as the accept button.
    34	2. A separate, explicit permission to collect from the wallet.
    35	3. Verification shown up front, so unverified users don't start an application.
    36	4. No default amount, and no urgency.
    37	
    38	## Why someone ends up late
    39	Repayment is collected on payday once salary has landed, at a fixed time (6pm). The reminder before the due date says exactly when. A borrower is only late if:
    40	- **payroll was delayed** (not their fault),
    41	- **they lost their job** (not their fault),
    42	- **their salary moved to a bank account**, or
    43	- **they spent the money before collection.**
    44	
    45	The first two aren't the user's fault, and that's why the late experience should be calm and practical, never accusing.
    46	
    47	**Due date vs salary arriving:** Days late are counted from 28 Jul, as the product reference says, and shown truthfully. The tone is calm from day 1. If payroll is delayed, the user can tell us and reminders pause.
    48	
    49	# Predatory behaviors we want to avoid
    50	
    51	**Entry**
    52	- Claiming an offer exists before eligibility is known.
    53	- Defaulting to the largest amount.
    54	- Countdown timers or "offer expires".
    55	- Asking for access to contacts, photos or SMS in exchange for a bigger limit. (Income documents to check affordability are fine. Personal data harvesting never is.)
    56	
    57	**Cost**
    58	- Showing the fee after commitment.
    59	- Hiding when and from where repayment is taken.
    60	- Calling it "no interest". The fee is a fixed 3% of the amount, charged once per advance. It isn't an annual rate.
    61	
    62	**Accept**
    63	- Pre-ticked consent.
    64	- A vague button that takes the loan.
    65	- Bundling permission to collect from the wallet into "I agree".
    66	- No record of what was agreed.
    67	
    68	**Decline**
    69	- A no with no reason.
    70	- Making people keep re-applying. Instead we re-check on a stated date, and they never need to apply again.
    71	
    72	**Late**
    73	- Contacting family, contacts or the employer.
    74	- Public shaming.
    75	- Debt details on the lock screen.
    76	- Constant notifications.
    77	- Freezing the wallet.
    78	- Paying a fee to push the date back (rollovers).
    79	- Taking the whole salary the moment it lands.
    80	- Threatening language.
    81	
    82	## Principles (each one can fail a screen)
    83	1. **The number you tap is the number you owe.** On the screen with the accept button, the amount received, the fee in rupees, the total and the due date are all visible without scrolling or tapping. The button names the amount, and its second line the repayment and date, unless the rest of the screen already makes those clear enough that the line would only repeat them.
    84	2. **Know before you ask.** No user reaches a "no" that could have been known before they applied. Only the credit check happens at application.
    85	3. **Smaller is never harder.** Tiers in ascending order, nothing pre-selected, the same visual weight for each, no timers, no expiry.
    86	4. **Late is a situation, not a character flaw.**
    87	   - At most 2 reminders a week.
    88	   - None between 10pm and 8am.
    89	   - No amount, "loan" or "overdue" on the lock screen.
    90	   - Never sent to anyone but the borrower.
    91	   - Red only on the event that failed (e.g. "We couldn't collect on 28 Jul"), never on the person's status card or the late screen. Their status uses the attention colour.
    92	   - Attention colour: the amber ramp, now named `attention`, only as a soft background with dark text (body text neutral-900 on attention-50; attention-600 only for the short status label). Never a solid fill, never on headlines, no alarm icons.
    93	5. **Their wallet stays theirs.** The advance is shown separately from their own money. Collection only ever takes what's owed, attempted once each time salary lands, never on a daily loop (whether retries are allowed is an open question). The wallet is never frozen. 
    94	
    95	## A moment that shouldn't exist
    96	**"Declined: income unverified."**
    97	- Assuming verification status is known before anyone applies (see Assumptions), the home card can show verification as a step to complete first, instead of letting the user apply and then declining them: "Verify your salary to unlock an advance", with the steps.
    98	- No application is made, so no decline is recorded.
    99	- **Counter-argument I accept:** using wallet data to pre-screen needs the user's consent, and the backend's decline reason would need to change. It's a product change, not just copy.
   100	
   101	## Scope
   102	Built as separate states the reviewer can jump to, so the depth goes into two places.
   103	
   104	**In depth: terms + accept**
   105	- Tiers with the fee in rupees, the total and the date. The over-limit tier is shown blocked, with the reason.
   106	- What happens if it's late, in one line, with the details in a bottom sheet. Default consequences are stated here, at accept, as in my Assumptions.
   107	- A separate collection permission, its own unticked checkbox, that doesn't repeat the amounts above it: "I allow NovaPay to take the repayment above automatically." with "This ends automatically when it's repaid, or on 27 Aug at the latest." On a lower offer it says "the new repayment".
   108	- A descriptive button: "Accept Rs 10,000". No second line on S4, because "Your advance" above it already shows "You repay on 28 Jul" and Rs 10,300 without scrolling.
   109	- After the tap: processing, double-tap protection, network failure, and a reduced payout that needs fresh consent.
   110	- A receipt of what was agreed.
   111	
   112	**In depth: the late path (my one bad-news path)**
   113	Reminder before the due date → Not collected on payday → late → notice before default.
   114	
   115	Causes of "Not collected on payday": salary didn't arrive, salary arrived short of Rs 10,300, balance dropped below Rs 10,300 before 6pm, or salary moved to a bank account.
   116	
   117	**Thin**
   118	The home card: eligible vs needs verification (the second persona's home-card state). The rest of the "shouldn't exist" case is argued here in writing.
   119	
   120	Home after accepting: their own balance first, with the advance shown separately. This is where the receipt's Done goes, and it makes principle 5 testable.
   121	
   122	**With more time**
   123	Credit-history decline, the default screen itself, successful repayment, viewing the advance later, early repayment. Modelling spending, so the balance always shows how much of it is borrowed.
   124	
   125	## First impressions of NovaKit
   126	- Card and Panel are the same component; only the border differs, and Card's border is a hardcoded colour.
   127	- The secondary button's grey text makes it look disabled. On an accept screen, the "no" option would look unavailable.
   128	- The only status colour is success. Amber is labelled "for expressive moments" and has no defined meaning, so anyone would grab it for a late screen. I'll give it one meaning (attention) with rules, or not use it.
   129	- Toast is success-only.
   130	- There's no checkbox or radio button.
   131	- There's no error colour, which the failure states will need.
   132	- Button has a fixed height and 20px text at large size. A descriptive label like "Accept Rs 10,000 · repay Rs 10,300 on 28 Jul" probably won't fit. I'd rather change Button (a secondary line and a minimum height) than loosen principle 1. The audit will confirm.
   133	
   134	The full audit against my scope comes next (docs/01-system-audit.md).
   135	
   136	## Assumptions
   137	- The user is salaried, with a limit of Rs 10,000. Salary of Rs 68,000 lands in NovaPay on the 28th. Today is 7 Jul, so the advance is due 28 Jul (21 days).
   138	- The fee is 3% of the amount paid out, charged once, and added to the repayment.
   139	- A second user is paid into a bank account, so the wallet can't see their income. They see the "Verify your salary" home card.
   140	- Wallet balance is Rs 4,250 for both personas (taken from the starter screen).
   141	- The payout lands in the NovaPay wallet the moment the advance is accepted, so the receipt can say "Rs 10,000 is in your NovaPay wallet".
   142	- Verification status is known before applying. The product reference says income may or may not be verified at application, so this is my assumption.
   143	- Collection is automatic, from the NovaPay wallet, on payday once salary has landed, at a fixed time (6pm), with explicit and separate permission given at accept. The reminder before the due date says exactly when. Collection is attempted only when salary lands, never from other incoming money.
   144	- Automatic collection is full amount only. The user can choose to pay part manually (shown on the late screen, stubbed in the prototype).
   145	- Reminder before the due date: 25 Jul at 10:00. The not-collected notice: 6pm on the day the attempt fails.
   146	- Late reminders every 7 days (4, 11, 18 and 25 Aug). This cadence is a placeholder.
   147	- Notice before default: 20 Aug, never paused, even after a payroll delay is reported. Default happens on day 30 (27 Aug).
   148	- A reduced payout always drops to a lower tier (e.g. 10,000 → 5,000), so the fee is always a whole number of rupees. It needs fresh consent to the new terms. A reduced payout can't go below Rs 5,000, the lowest tier. That case isn't designed.
   149	- After a default, new advances are paused and the wallet is never frozen.
   150	- After default, automatic collection stops. We ask for permission again, or the user pays manually.
   151	- Default consequences shown in the prototype are only the ones above: new advances are paused, automatic collection stops, and the wallet is never frozen. They're shown as stated, without a placeholder label. Anything else (credit reporting, collections, legal steps) isn't shown until compliance confirms it.
   152	- Data uses the glossary field names. The screens say "declined".
   153	- **What I'd push for, pending finance and compliance:** no late fees and no compounding. The screens won't promise "never" until it's confirmed.
   154	
   155	## What I'd want to know
   156	- Is there a required cancellation window?
   157	- Is the fee legally interest? Do we need a key facts statement? Is interest (riba) a concern for this market?
   158	- What exactly happens at default: which credit bureau, collections, any legal steps?
   159	- Should a reported payroll delay move the default date?
   160	- Collection: can we retry when funds are short? How often? Is any amount protected for the user?
   161	- What happens if a reduced payout is needed from the lowest tier?
   162	- How is the limit set?
   163	- How long can a collection permission legally last, and what does re-asking after default require?
   164	- Can we use wallet data to check eligibility before an application, and what consent does that need?
   165	- How is the record of agreement delivered and stored, and in which languages (Urdu and English)?
   166	- Why are people actually late (payroll delays, job loss, spending)? What does the data say?
   167	- Does a re-check after a decline hit the credit bureau?
   168	- The product reference cites "Trust rules" that don't exist, and its decision wording isn't consistent. Which is the source of truth?
   169	
   170	## How I'd know it's good (60–90 days)
   171	- **Understanding:** when asked right after accepting, borrowers can state what they'll repay and when.
   172	- **Fewer support contacts** about fees and the due date.
   173	- **The spread of amounts chosen doesn't drift towards the maximum.**
   174	- **Late borrowers contact us or repay** rather than going quiet. Complaints about reminders and opt-outs stay low.
   175	- **Repeat borrowing:** how often someone borrows again within 7 days of repaying. It should stay low.
   176	- **What it should never do,** whatever it does to conversion:
   177	  - contact anyone other than the borrower,
   178	  - freeze the wallet,
   179	  - take more than what's owed,
   180	  - hide the cost until after the user commits.
   181	
   182	
   183	  ## Response to the AI critique
   184	| Point | My call | Why |
   185	|---|---|---|

   187	| The entry card diagnosis was backwards | Accept | "See your offer" is the claim |
   188	| No "what's working" and no position on conversion | Accept | Both added |
   189	| Why someone ends up late | Accept | It decides the tone. A grace rule was added in v2, then removed in round 2: days late are shown truthfully. |
   190	| Contradictions (salary sweep, personal info, red) | Accept | Lines drawn in the principles |
   191	| Separate permission to collect from the wallet | Accept | Becomes the checkbox, so consent is specific rather than a generic "I agree" |
   192	| Default consequences at accept | Accept | One line plus details |
   193	| The limit grows after on-time repayments | Accept, removed | It rewards repeat borrowing |
   194	| No cancellation window | Adapt | Moved to "want to know" |
   195	| "No late fees, ever" | Adapt | "Pushing for, pending confirmation" |
   196	| Cut v1's separate "Record of the advance" screen | Accept | Moved to "With more time" |
   197	| Your suggested late path left out the reminder before the due date | **Reject** | It's the one chance to prevent two of the four causes of lateness: salary moved to a bank, and money spent before collection |
   198	| Keep a receipt after accepting (my addition, not a critique point) | Keep | The accept moment isn't finished until the user knows it worked. It will say where the lasting record lives, which is still an open question |
   199	| Round 2: my reasons for the receipt and the reminder were weak | Accept | Reasons replaced, see the two rows above |
   200	| Cut the credit decline, default screen, success screen | Accept | Moved to "with more time" |

   204	|---|---|---|

   209	| Default consequences at accept are things I don't know yet | Accept | Marked as placeholder copy until compliance confirms, and listed as an assumption |

   211	| Principle 5 had no screen to fail on | Accept | Added home after accepting, where the receipt's Done goes |

content.content:
### Chat 1: project setup

- **Flattened the zip's `novakit-lite/` folder into the repo root** so the repo is the project itself, with no extra folder level.
- **Kept the zip out of the repo with `.git/info/exclude`, not `.gitignore`,** so the only change to the starter's `.gitignore` is the `_inputs/` line that was asked for.
- **Kept `brief.md` inside `_inputs/`** so it's covered by the same ignore rule and the brief is never published.
- **Did not run `npm audit fix`,** even though the install reported 14 vulnerabilities (4 moderate, 10 high). Fixing them would change the starter's lockfile.
- **Wrote `brief.md` as Markdown that follows the PDF's layout.** The boxed sections became blockquotes, the page footers were dropped, and the sentence split across pages 1 and 2 was joined.
- **Used a Stop hook rather than UserPromptSubmit for the prompt log.** Stop doesn't fire on an interrupt, so cancelled prompts stay out of the log.
- **Gave each logged prompt and session a hidden ID marker.** This means a prompt is never logged twice, and sessions stay grouped even when they alternate.
- **Wrote the hook in Node** because Python isn't installed on this machine.

### Chat 2: critique of my read, and rails

- **Scope is depth in two places:** terms + accept, and the late path (reminder before the due date → not collected on payday → late → notice before default). The home card (eligible vs needs verification) and home after accepting are thin. The credit decline, default screen, successful repayment and viewing the advance later are cut.
- **"Declined: income unverified" shouldn't exist.** Verification becomes a step on the home card before anyone applies. This rests on an assumption that verification status is known before applying.
- **Kept the receipt after accepting:** the accept moment isn't finished until the user knows it worked.
- **Kept the reminder before the due date:** it's the one chance to prevent two of the causes of lateness.
- **No grace rule:** days late are counted from the due date and shown truthfully.
- **Attention colour (provisional):** the existing amber ramp, soft background with dark text (accent-600 on accent-50). The system audit confirms it.
- **Change Button rather than loosen principle 1:** the accept button needs a secondary line for the repayment and date. The audit confirms it.
- **The check catches hex colours and arbitrary values only,** in `src/`. The phone frame and the page backdrop behind it are allowed.
- **The starter's hard-coded colours are allow-listed as starter debt, not fixed.** Fixing them is a token or component change, which is my call. Each entry is labelled to be removed once the fix lands.
- **The prompt log keeps every prompt,** including near-duplicate resends, so it matches its own "every prompt" claim.

### Chat 3: system audit

The full record is in the "My decision" column of `docs/01-system-audit.md`. None of these is built yet.

- **Button evolves:** a second line in brand-100, a minimum height, a loading state, and secondary text in neutral-900. The "no" option must be as clear as "yes".
- **One new component, `Choice`** (native checkbox and radio). The blocked tier stays visible, with its reason in neutral-700.
- **Choosing the amount and terms + accept are two screens,** so the full cost is visible without scrolling.
- **Accept stays enabled.** Tapping it without the permission shows a neutral inline message at the checkbox. A disabled button doesn't explain itself, and nothing has failed. *Chat 4: the message moved to the action area, above Accept.*
- **AmountText:** a missing amount renders nothing and the screen says "not available yet". It inherits its colour, and gets a caption size and an optional sign.
- **accent is renamed to attention:**
  - body text is neutral-900 on attention-50,
  - attention-600 is only for the short status label,
  - DEFAULT is removed: nothing uses it, and removing it makes a solid amber fill impossible,
  - 100 is kept, documented as not for text.
- **New tokens `danger` #B42318 and `danger-50` #FEF3F2.** Card gets a tone (default, attention or danger). Failures are inline Cards with `role="alert"`, never a Toast.
- **Retune at the source:** neutral-500 to #6B6B6B, which fixes every caption at once, and success to #15803D.

## Write-up inbox

### Assumptions

The full list is in `docs/00-my-read.md` → Assumptions. The ones that most need defending:

- Verification status is known before anyone applies (the product reference says it may be checked at application).
- Collection is automatic, on payday at 6pm once salary has landed, with its own permission given at accept.
- Automatic collection is full amount only; the user can choose to pay part manually.
- The collection permission ends when the advance is repaid or at the default date, whichever comes first.
- Default consequences shown in the prototype are only: new advances paused, automatic collection stops, the wallet never frozen. Shown as stated, no placeholder label (changed in chat 4).
- A reduced payout always drops to a lower tier (e.g. 10,000 → 5,000), so the fee is always a whole number of rupees, and it needs fresh consent.
- Pushing for, pending finance and compliance: no late fees and no compounding.
- *Added in chat 3, continued:*
  - Collection is attempted only when salary lands, never from other incoming money.
  - Reminders:
    - 25 Jul at 10:00,
    - the not-collected notice at 6pm when the attempt fails,
    - late reminders every 7 days (placeholder cadence),
    - the notice before default on 20 Aug, never paused,
    - default on day 30 (27 Aug).
  - Wallet balance is Rs 4,250 for both personas.
  - A reduced payout can't go below Rs 5,000. That case isn't designed.
  - The payout lands in the NovaPay wallet the moment the advance is accepted (added in chat 4).

### What I'd want to know

The full list is in `docs/00-my-read.md` → What I'd want to know. The ones that most shape the build:

- Is there a required cancellation window?
- Is the fee legally interest? Do we need a key facts statement?
- What exactly happens at default (credit bureau, collections, legal steps)?
- Can collection retry when funds are short, and is any amount protected?
- How long can a collection permission legally last?
- *Added in chat 3, continued:*
  - Should a reported payroll delay move the default date?
  - What happens if a reduced payout is needed from the lowest tier?
- *Added in chat 4:*
  - How is the limit set?

### System flags

- Card and Panel are the same component; only the border differs.
- Hard-coded colours: Card's border `#E6E6E6`, ListRow's border `#DADADA`, and `#1a1a1a` in `index.css` (duplicates neutral-900).
- The secondary button's grey text (neutral-500) makes it look disabled, so the "no" option on an accept screen would look unavailable. It's also 3.95:1 on white, which fails WCAG AA at 15px. Captions and placeholders use the same grey, so the fine print on the accept screen would be the least readable text.
- The only status colour is success. There's no warning, error or info, and the amber accent has no defined meaning.
- Toast is success-only and has no `aria-live`. White on the success green is 3.45:1, which fails AA. (Correction: the 2.2s dismiss is in `App.jsx:25`, not in Toast.)
- TextField has no label, error state or helper text, and its border is 1.41:1, too faint to show where the input is.
- BottomSheet has no dialog role, focus trap or Escape handling, and tapping the backdrop closes it. Its grab handle suggests a swipe that isn't built.
- Button has a fixed height, 56px at large size, so the two-line accept label (about 64px) doesn't fit. It's also always full-width, has no loading state and no designed focus style.
- AmountText renders "Rs 0" when the amount is missing, which breaks my own rule. It forces `text-neutral-900`, so an amount inside a primary button would be 2.77:1. It has no caption size and no sign.
- There's no checkbox or radio button.
- Colours sit under `extend`, so Tailwind's whole default palette (`red-500`, `amber-400`…) is still available, and the first version of the check didn't see it. The starter also uses `bg-white`, `text-white`, `bg-black/40` and `shadow-xl`.
- No component forwards extra props, so none can take an `id`, `role` or `aria-*` attribute without being edited.
- ListRow truncates its title and subtitle, which would cut cost and due-date lines.
- The phone frame grows with its content, so "visible without scrolling" can't be tested, and Toast and BottomSheet can end up off-screen.
- The amber ramp: accent-600 on accent-50 is 4.71:1, a pass by 0.21. accent-600 fails on accent-100 (4.31) and neutral-100 (4.49). accent DEFAULT fails as text (2.15).
- After the accent → attention rename, the README's example `text-accent-600` will be out of date. *(Fixed in chat 3.)*
- *Added in chat 3, continued, found while changing the system:*
  - **The dev server keeps the old Tailwind config.** After a change to `tailwind.config.js` it served stale CSS until it was restarted.
  - **The check only knows the names it's given.** It catches Tailwind's default colour names but not ones that don't exist, which build silently.
  - **Exporting a helper from a `.jsx` file** (`formatAmount` from `AmountText.jsx`) costs Vite's fast refresh for that file, so edits reload the whole page.
  - **Native checkbox and radio rendering varies by browser,** so check `Choice`'s 24px control and focus ring on each.
  - **The "‹" glyph was about 5px wide at the inherited 16px,** even inside a 44px target.
  - **On Windows the frame's scroll area showed a classic scrollbar.** It's now hidden.
  - ~~**The README prose still says "a warm amber accent"** after the rename.~~ *Resolved in chat 4: the README's palette and file list describe the kit as it is now.*
- *Added in chat 4, found while building S3 and S4:*
  - **The browser pane's accessibility tree isn't the browser's.** It named radios by their `value` and gave buttons no name. Real names came from Edge's tree over the DevTools protocol.
  - **A natively disabled radio is invisible to keyboard users.** Tab and the arrow keys skip it, so its reason is never heard. Choice now uses `aria-disabled`.
  - **A button's two lines ran together as one name** ("Review terms Nothing is borrowed yet"). Button now adds a stop between them.
  - **Toast was success-only,** so "you can't choose that" would have worn a green tick. It now has a `neutral` variant. It still has no `aria-live`.
  - **The dev server's file watcher missed edits twice** and served old files until it was restarted.
  - **The fixed 390×844 frame hid a small-phone problem.** At 360×640, S3's first card pushed every amount below the fold.
  - **Advance IDs contain the year,** so they can't be shown on screen.
  - **The starter BottomSheet couldn't be used as it was.** It had no dialog role, focus handling or Escape, and its grab handle promised a swipe that didn't exist. It was rebuilt before S4 used it.
  - **`aria-modal` alone doesn't stop focus leaving a sheet.** The rest of the frame had to be made `inert`.
  - **Large buttons don't fit two to a row at 390px.** "Change amount" wrapped onto two lines.
  - **`formatAmount` uses a non-breaking space** between "Rs" and the number, so a plain-space text search ("Accept Rs 5,000") misses it.
  - **Background browser tabs pause `requestAnimationFrame` and throttle timers.** A scroll put in a rAF never ran there, so it now uses a timeout.
  - **`inert` is passed as `inert=""`,** which React 18 renders. React 19 expects a boolean, so it needs changing on an upgrade.

### AI process

- **Stopped the AI working ahead.** I opened chat 3 by only saying what it would cover. The AI started reading every file and was about to run the build. I stopped it and said not to start the audit yet.
- **Triage by short codes.** The AI sorted 122 audit rows into 26 safe defaults and 14 questions with lettered options. I answered with codes and one-line reasons.
- **Overrode the AI's recommendation on accent DEFAULT.** It said keep it, documented as never for text. I removed it, so a solid amber fill can't happen.
- **The AI flagged a gap in my own answer.** My first answer on the check (14A) didn't say whether `white` and `black` count. The AI recorded it as open instead of guessing, and I decided it: `white`, `black` and `transparent` are allowed.
- **The audit narrowed my read.** The attention-colour wording in principle 4 became "body text neutral-900, accent-600 only for the label". I accepted it and updated the read.
- *Added in chat 3, continued:*
  - **Rejected AI output (candidate for the write-up).** The AI's first module paused every reminder after a payroll delay, including the notice before default. I changed it: that notice is never paused, because a material consequence must always be announced. A check now guards it.
  - **Reworked AI output.** The AI's wallet said "Includes Rs 10,000 from your advance" on every day. I limited it to home after accepting, because once money is spent the claim isn't true and spending isn't modelled.
  - **The AI caught a contradiction in my spec.** I asked for every reminder at 10:00, but the not-collected notice can't go out before the 6pm attempt. I confirmed 6pm.
  - **The AI's own suggestion failed when measured.** `text-title` for the back glyph barely helped, so it used `text-display` and said why.
  - **Proving the rails work:**
    - each check was shown failing on a deliberate mutation,
    - each component change was measured before and after in the running app,
    - every temporary probe was removed.
  - **The AI attributed a rule to my read that isn't there:** "the payout lands when accepted". It was caught while writing this file and is now an open question.
- *Added in chat 4:*
  - **Rejected AI output (candidate for the write-up).** The AI's first over-limit reason added a placeholder about how the limit is set ("based on your salary and how you use NovaPay"). I cut it: it's invented policy, and it hints that activity earns a bigger limit.
  - **A three-way critique, then triage by codes.** The AI critiqued S3 as a regulator, a low-literacy borrower and a screen-reader user. I sorted every point into fix, reject or defer, with reasons. The rejections are in Pushback.
  - **"Check first" paid off.** I asked for the accessible names before any fix. The browser pane's tree said the radios were named "5000"; Edge's real tree said "Rs 5,000". Fixing the pane's reading would have been wasted work.
  - **The AI asked before using the existing Toast.** It was green with a tick, which would have contradicted the message. I chose a neutral variant.
  - **Copy measured, not guessed.** For the small-phone fold, the AI tried each card draft in the live screen at 360×640 and reported the pixels. The heading alone cost 22px.
  - **The AI caught my S3 copy contradicting my own flow.** "We'll confirm the final amount before you accept" didn't match a reduced payout arriving after the tap. I changed it.
  - **The AI found two issues in its own build:** the toast covered the way out, and the dimmed radio dimmed its own focus ring. Both were fixed before commit.
  - **Overrides I made:** no annual rate on S4 (the fee is a fixed 3%), no late-fee or "being confirmed" lines, and no placeholder label on the default line. I then updated my Assumptions and the audit to match.
  - **The AI pushed back on my checkbox wording.** I asked for "I have read the terms stated above and accept". The AI pointed out that this is the bundled "I agree" on my own predatory list, and it breaks my `CLAUDE.md` rule. My real point was not repeating the amounts, so the checkbox now points at "the repayment above" and stays its own permission with an end date.
  - **A review agent re-verified S4 against every doc.** It found a false promise (retrying "when your salary next arrives", which lands after default for most causes), the checkbox state never reaching the module, an incomplete focus trap, a 22px target, and the AI's own S5/S8 mislabel. All were fixed, and its other points became decisions or doc updates.
  - **No commits until I say "Commit now".** The AI kept the S4 redesign in the working tree while I iterated.
  - **A second review agent checked S5–S7 against every doc.** The AI's own copy had three problems:
    - "Check your connection" blamed the user,
    - "After our final checks" stated a policy I hadn't written,
    - S7 hid where the repayment is taken from.
    It also caught a reviewer control that didn't do what its label said. All were fixed.
  - **I rejected the AI's table on S7** and asked for the same list rows as S4, so old and new read the same way as the screen before.

### Deferred from the S3 critique

- **R9:** lender name, key facts and cancellation. It's a "want to know"; a placeholder lender line on S4 comes later.
- **B3:** a test at 200% text size.
- **B10:** Urdu. The prototype is English only for now.
- **SR9:** how abbreviations ("Rs", "Jul", "6pm") are read aloud.

### Pushback

Critique points I rejected, with my reasons.

- **S3 critique, R6: say what happens if salary doesn't land.** S4 is the commitment point and covers it. Putting it here makes S3 longer, which the critique's own B2 says is already a problem.
- **S3 critique, R7: the blocked Rs 15,000 works as an anchor.** Showing the limit honestly is the over-limit moment the brief asks for. There's no "unlock" language, and it sits last, in ascending order. Hiding it would be less transparent.
- **S3 critique, R8: "Nothing is borrowed yet" lowers resistance.** It's true, and it sits on "Review terms", not on the commit button. Saying what hasn't happened yet lowers pressure; it doesn't lower scrutiny.
- **S3 critique, SR6: the terms sit outside the form.** Reading order reaches the card before the choices. Moving the card into the form wouldn't help anyone.

## Next step

S3 to S9 are built. S9 and the details view are in the working tree, waiting for my "Commit now". After that come the reviewer switcher and the late path.

## Review of S8, S9, AdvanceDetails and the related docs (read-only)

`npm run build` and `npm run check` both pass (token check clean; 29 advance checks). I changed no files.

### Findings, most important first

**1. High (code + doc): "Home never offers a second advance" is a policy that isn't written down, and it's enforced in the screen, not the module.**
- `src/screens/Home.jsx:8` says "Home never offers a second advance on top of an open one". Line 29 enforces it with `advance ? … : offer card`. The audit S9 note (`docs/01-system-audit.md:38`) records it: "replaces the offer card, so home never offers a second advance".
- Neither `PRODUCT_REFERENCE.md` nor the Assumptions say one advance at a time.
- `getOffer` (`salaryAdvance.js:125`) still returns `eligible` with the full limit while an advance is open. So the limit rule now lives in a screen, which goes against CLAUDE.md "All salary-advance logic lives in one module … the limit".
- Fix: the owner adds an Assumption, and `getOffer` takes the open advance and returns, say, an `has_advance` state.

**2. Medium/High (code copy + doc): the receipt's record line doesn't match what it points to, and states something not in the Assumptions.**
- `Receipt.jsx:41` says "You can open this any time from your advance on Home." But "See details" opens a different view, not "this". The owner chose "a details view of the terms (not the confirmation screen)".
- "Any time" is a promise nothing defines. Home's card is only shown while `advance` exists, and nothing is defined after repayment.
- "Home" is capitalised as a place name, but no screen is labelled Home: the AppBar says "NovaPay" and back buttons say "Back to home".
- "The record lives in the app" is only in `progress.md:287/300`, not the Assumptions. CLAUDE.md: "Any copy that states a policy must match my Assumptions."
- The read's want-to-know (`00-my-read.md:165`) still asks "How is the record of agreement delivered and stored".
- Fix: the owner adds an Assumption and rewords the line to point at "See details", for example "You can see these details from your advance on the home screen."

**3. Medium (doc): `progress.md` contradicts the latest decision about signs.**
- `docs/progress.md:287`: "Only the advance row gets a sign; the starter rows follow the current design."
- `progress.md:153`: "The starter rows are unchanged."
- The code (`Home.jsx:71,77,83`) and the owner's decision put a sign on every row.
- The audit S9 note (`:38`) doesn't mention the starter rows' signs.
- Fix: update all three.

**4. Medium (code, not reachable today): a missing balance shows an empty balance card.**
- `getWallet` returns `balance: null` on any day other than `received_on` (`salaryAdvance.js:371`). `Home.jsx:20` then shows "Available balance" with nothing under it.
- Audit 6.1's decision says "The screen says 'not available yet'".
- It can't happen in the app now, because `today` is fixed to 7 Jul. It will happen once the planned reviewer switcher puts Home on S10–S13 (25 Jul onward).
- In the same states, the advance card would still say "to repay on 28 Jul" and "We take it … at 6pm". After repayment it would say "Rs 0 to repay" (`status.outstanding`).
- Fix: Home shows a "not available yet" line when `balance == null`, or Home is limited to S1/S9.

**5. Medium (code): the screens decide dates and times themselves.**
- `Home.jsx:63`: `advance.received_on === today ? "Today" : formatDate(...)` is a date comparison in a screen. CLAUDE.md: "Screens never calculate money or dates themselves."
- `Receipt.jsx:32` says "It's in your NovaPay wallet now." regardless of `received_on`, which the module provides.
- Fix: the module provides a relative-day label, or a `received_today` flag.

**6. Medium (owner decision, doc vs build): principle 5 against the balance shown first.**
- The read says "Home after accepting: their own balance first, with the advance shown separately" (`00-my-read.md:120`). Principle 5 (`:93`) says "The advance is shown separately from their own money." Audit S9's need (`:38`) says "Own balance first."
- The build shows Rs 14,250 (own money plus the advance) as "Available balance" in `display` size. The borrowed share is only a caption, "Includes Rs 10,000 from your advance".
- This matches the getWallet decision. But the read's "own balance first" wording now contradicts it.
- Fix: the owner either rewords Thin and the audit, or shows own and borrowed separately.

**7. Medium (code): "Your advance" is used twice on the details screen.**
- `AdvanceDetails.jsx:22`: AppBar `<h1>` "Your advance". `advanceParts.jsx:24`: AdvanceSummary `<h2>` "Your advance", on the same screen.
- Home's card for the same thing is "Your salary advance" (`Home.jsx:32`).
- Fix: rename one. For example, title the screen "Your salary advance", or give AdvanceSummary a heading prop.

**8. Medium (owner's doc, the read): it still says the advance view and the record are future work, and that the receipt holds the agreement.**
- `00-my-read.md:123` (With more time): "viewing the advance later". It's now built (AdvanceDetails).
- `:196` (critique table): "Cut v1's separate 'Record of the advance' screen | Accept | Moved to 'With more time'". That's effectively what AdvanceDetails now is.
- `:198`: "where the lasting record lives, which is still an open question". It's now decided.
- `:110` (Scope, in depth): "A receipt of what was agreed." The receipt no longer shows the terms; the details view does.
- `progress.md:174` (chat 2 decision) also says "viewing the advance later are cut".
- Fix: the owner updates Scope and adds a note to the table. It's the owner's file, so I didn't touch it.

**9. Low (doc): the audit's S8 row is stale.**
- `01-system-audit.md:37` says "then the record as a labelled placeholder". The placeholder label is gone.
- `progress.md:144` (the S8 section) says the same thing. That's acceptable as history, but the S9 section's second "Checked in the app" bullet (`:157`) is about S8 and sits under S9.

**10. Low (code): the same fact is worded differently across screens.**
- S8: "You received" (`Receipt.jsx:28`). Activity row: "Advance received". Details reuses S4's "You get" (`advanceParts.jsx:28`), which is the future tense for something already received.
- "Accepted on 7 Jul" is caption text inside a card on S8 (`Receipt.jsx:33`), but "Accepted on 7 Jul." is body text with a full stop, outside any card, on details (`AdvanceDetails.jsx:25`).
- On details, LateLine sits inside the "Your permission" card (`:41`). On S4 it has its own card, and the late line isn't about the permission.

**11. Low (code): the receipt's repayment line doesn't say where the money is taken from.**
- `Receipt.jsx:36-39`: "You repay Rs 10,300 on 28 Jul at 6pm, once your salary arrives." There's no "from your NovaPay wallet".
- S7 was fixed for exactly this ("S7 now says where the repayment comes from"), and Home's card (`Home.jsx:38`) and S4 both say it.

**12. Low (code): sample data in Home is still hard-coded.**
- "Salary credited / 28 Jun / +Rs 68,000" (`Home.jsx:75-78`) hard-codes persona A's salary and payday, which the module has.
- I17 named "salary 68,000" specifically, and its new note (`audit:216`) only says the balance was moved.
- "Today, 2:14 PM" (`:70`) uses a different time format from the module's `formatTime` ("6pm", "2:14pm").
- "Mobile top-up" has no word for direction. Home's docstring (`:11-12`) says "Every row shows its direction in words and a sign", and audit 6.18 says "Words … plus the `sign` option".

**13. Low (code): caption colours and headings on Home differ from the other screens.**
- "Available balance" and "Recent activity" use `text-neutral-500` (`Home.jsx:18,58`). The "Includes…" line in the same card (`:23`) and every other screen's captions use `neutral-700`.
- "Recent activity" and the offer card's "Need cash before payday?" (`:48`) are `<div>`s, but the advance card's title is an `<h2>`, so the heading outline changes between S1 and S9.
- The S1 entry button is `size="lg"` (`:51`), but S9's "See details" in the same slot is md.

**14. Low (code comment and docs that name old places).**
- `advanceParts.jsx:5-6` says the parts are shared by "S4, S7 and the receipt (S8)". The receipt no longer uses them; AdvanceDetails does.
- `progress.md:147` says the parts are "used by S4 and S7", and leaves out AdvanceDetails.
- Audit I14 and I17 still point to `App.jsx:…` lines; the code is now in `Home.jsx`.
- The audit's ListRow and cost-row tables list S8, which no longer uses ListRow.
- `progress.md:329-330`: struck items keep trailing text that now contradicts them ("This waits for home after accepting (S9)", "it isn't done").

**15. Low (doc): the read's Assumption quotes copy the receipt doesn't use.**
- `00-my-read.md:141` quotes the receipt as saying "Rs 10,000 is in your NovaPay wallet". The build says "It's in your NovaPay wallet now."

**16. Low (doc): the Write-up inbox has nothing from S8 or S9.**
- Missing: the record lives in the app, the one-advance rule (if adopted), the move to signs on every row, and the "Includes" line being for the payout day only. CLAUDE.md asks for these at the end of the chat.

**17. Low (reviewer scaffolding).**
- After one accept, home hides the entry card, so the reviewer can't re-run S4–S8 with another outcome without reloading the page. The "Reviewer: after Accept" control stays visible and does nothing.
- The untracked `vite.config.js.timestamp-….mjs` is a Vite temp file, and `.gitignore` doesn't cover it, so it shouldn't be committed.

### Checked and consistent
- No hex or arbitrary values in the new screens; `text-brand`, `display` and the other tokens are used correctly. No NovaKit files changed, so no `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` entry is needed.
- S8 matches the owner's intent: one centred column, the amount in `display` size and brand colour, no success colour, no confetti, no back, Done goes home, and no placeholder label.
- The balance comes from `getWallet` before and after accepting (4,250, then 14,250). The advance card reads `getStatus().outstanding`, `due_date` and `collection.time`. The "Includes" line is shown only when `includes_advance != null`.
- Every activity row has a sign. `formatAmount` turns `"-"` into U+2212. The arrow glyphs are `aria-hidden` (ListRow). Whether every screen reader reads U+2212 aloud is still untested in a real one.
